# Overview

## Code Description

This script contains code that imports the Master database for the Brain Health at Midlife and Menopause (BHAMM) Study, filters out participants that do not meet the relevant inclusion/exclusion criteria (for BHAMM and for this specific project), and then outputs data for later analyses.

Input(s):

  * SPSS file of the BHAMM Master database (Last updated: November 2024)

Output(s):

  * SPSS file containing cleaned Session 2 (behavioral task) data.
  * SPSS file containing cleaned Session 2 (imaging) data for CS analysis.
  * SPSS file containing cleaned Session 2 (imaging) data for CR analysis.
  
Note: Identifiable information (e.g., file names, subject IDs) have been replaced by placeholders (e.g., subject IDs appear as XXXX).
  
# Packages

Load all required packages.
```{r}
# package versions are listed to aid de-bugging - you should not need these exact versions
library(haven) # version 2.5.4
library(janitor) # version 2.2.0
library(tidyr) # version 1.3.1
library(dplyr) # version 1.1.4
library(stringr) # version 1.5.1
```

# Import Data

Import the BHAMM study Master database and "clean" the variable names (i.e., make them all lower-case with spaces replaced by underscores, etc).
```{r}
bhamm <- read_sav("insert-file-name.sav") %>% clean_names() 
```

# General BHAMM Exclusions

Filter out participants who were listed as Session 1 exclusions. In doing so, this will remove anyone who should have been excluded at enrolment and/or Session 1.
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(bhamm, s1_exclude == 1) 
```

Optional: check the reasons for exclusion, consult the variable `s1_behav_issues_notes` for hints.
```{r}
# s1_issues <- bhamm %>% filter(s1_exclude == -1) %>% select(id, s1_behav_issues_notes)
```

Filter out participants who were older than 65 years of age at Session 1.
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, s1_age < 65) 
```

Filter out participants who reported undergoing a bilateral oophorectomy.
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, !enrol_ovaries %in% c(3, 4)) 
```

Filter out participants who reported having hypertension at enrolment or study, were not taking relevant meds, and have objective measures showing hypertension.
```{r}
# identify participants who said yes to hypertension at enrolment or later 
session_1 %>% count(enrol_med_cond_hypertension, med_con_hypertension)

# identify participants who said yes at enrolment OR at study AND said no to every relevant medicine at enrolment AND at study (relevant medicines identified through Mayo Clinic)
hyper_ids <- session_1 %>%
  filter(
    ((enrol_med_cond_hypertension %in% c(-1)) & (!enrol_meds_diuretic %in% c(-1) & 
                                                 !enrol_meds_ace_inhibitor %in% c(-1) & 
                                                 !enrol_meds_ar_bs %in% c(-1) & 
                                                 !enrol_meds_ccb %in% c(-1) & 
                                                 !enrol_meds_alpha_blockers %in% c(-1) &
                                                 !enrol_meds_statin %in% c(-1) &
                                                 !meds_diuretic %in% c(-1) & 
                                                 !meds_ace_inhibitor %in% c(-1) & 
                                                 !meds_arb %in% c(-1) & 
                                                 !meds_ccb %in% c(-1) & 
                                                 !meds_b_as %in% c(-1) &
                                                 !meds_statin %in% c(-1))) |
    ((med_con_hypertension %in% c(-1)) & (!enrol_meds_diuretic %in% c(-1) & 
                                          !enrol_meds_ace_inhibitor %in% c(-1) & 
                                          !enrol_meds_ar_bs %in% c(-1) & 
                                          !enrol_meds_ccb %in% c(-1) & 
                                          !enrol_meds_alpha_blockers %in% c(-1) & 
                                          !enrol_meds_statin %in% c(-1) &
                                          !meds_diuretic %in% c(-1) & 
                                          !meds_ace_inhibitor %in% c(-1) & 
                                          !meds_arb %in% c(-1) & 
                                          !meds_ccb %in% c(-1) & 
                                          !meds_b_as %in% c(-1) &
                                          !meds_statin %in% c(-1))))
  
# check whether these participants had high systolic blood pressure (>140mm/Hg)
hyper_ids %>% filter(bp_systolic_s1 > 140 | bp_systolic_s2)

# check whether these participants had high diastolic blood pressure (>90mm/Hg) 
hyper_ids %>% filter(bp_diastolic_s1 > 90 | bp_diastolic_s2 > 90) 

# check whether these participants had were coded as hypertensive
hyper_ids %>% filter(bp_coded_s1 == 4 | bp_coded_s2 == 4)

# check whether these participants have notes under Session 1 or Session 2 for uncontrolled hypertension
hyper_ids %>% filter(str_detect(s1_behav_issues_notes, "Uncontrolled") | str_detect(s2_issues_notes, "Uncontrolled")) 

# check if 5055 was listed as an exclusion at S1 or S2
hyper_ids %>% count(s1_exclude, s2_exclusion) 

# filter out the participant with uncontrolled hypertension
session_1 <- filter(session_1, id != XXXX) 
```

Filter out participants with diabetes.
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, !med_con_diabetes %in% c(-1))
```

Filter out participants with a history of estrogen-related cancers.
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, !enrol_med_cond_breast_cancer %in% c(-1) | !med_con_breast_cancer %in% c(-1))
```

Filter out participants with a neurological diagnosis.
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, !med_con_neurological %in% c(-1))
```

Filter out participants who smoke more than 40 cigarettes per day.
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, is.na(enrol_smoke_qty) | enrol_smoke_qty <= 40) 
session_1 <- filter(session_1, is.na(current_cigarettes_daily) | current_cigarettes_daily <= 40)
```

# Session 1 Exclusions

Because we used `s1_exclude` at the start of this script, it should have pulled out anyone who had an issue at enrolment and/or Session 1. After all, there are no data to analyse at enrolment alone. Nevertheless, it is worth checking these.

Filter out participants who have an MMSE score less than 26.
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, is.na(mmse) | mmse >= 26)
```

Filter out participants who have a MoCA score less than 19. Note: If there were participants with a score less than 19, we would need to check their ethnoracial group to ensure the appropriate cut-off has been used. 
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, is.na(moca) | moca >= 19)
```

Filter out participants who have a BDI-II score > 19.
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, is.na(bdi) | bdi <= 19) 
```

Filter out participants who have a BAI score > 21.
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, is.na(bai) | bai <= 21) 
```

Filter out participants who have more than 2 positive MINI modules.
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, is.na(mini) | mini < 3) 
```

# Study-Specific Exclusions

Filter out participants who were not middle-aged at both sessions.
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, s1_age_group == 2 & s2_age_group == 2)
```

Filter out males.
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, sex == 1) 
```

Given our focus on sex, filter out participants whose current gender identity does not match their sex assigned at birth. Note: for sex, labels are "-1 [Male]" and "1 [Female]"; for gender, labels are "1 [Man]" and "2 [Woman]".
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, (sex == -1 & enrol_gender == 1) | (sex == -1 & is.na(enrol_gender)) | (sex == 1 & enrol_gender == 2) | (sex == 1 & is.na(enrol_gender)))
```

Filter out participants whose BMI is greater than 40.
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, is.na(bmi) | bmi <= 40) 
```

Filter out participants whose menopause status at Session 1 and Session 2 is indeterminate.
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, !s1_meno_group %in% c(4) & !s2_meno_group %in% c(4))
```

Filter out participants for whom we do not have APOE e4 data.
```{r}
session_1 <- filter(session_1, !is.na(apoe4_allele)) 
```

# Session 2 Exclusions

Filter out participants for whom there is no session 2 date. This implies that they have not attended session 2 (i.e., the imaging session).
```{r}
session_2 <- filter(session_1, !is.na(s2_date))
```

Filter out those who are session 2 (MRI) exclusions. Specifically, those who are exclusions due to incidental findings, claustrophobia, or undisclosed medical conditions. 
```{r}
session_2 <- filter(session_2, !s2_reason_exclusion %in% c(1, 2, 4))
```

Filter out participants who are pregnant.
```{r}
session_2 <- filter(session_2, !pregnant_now %in% c(-1)) 
```

## Task fMRI Exclusions

Filter out participants who were scanned with old MRI parameters.
```{r}
session_2_task <- filter(session_2, !str_detect(s2_task_issues, "Old MRI Protocol")) 
```

The database includes incorrect values for sub-XXXX. Hard run 1 was excluded incorrectly from their onset file (checked separately). This has now been corrected but needs to be amended here.
```{r}
# check old CS rate and then replace
session_2_task$cs_rate_hard[session_2_task$id == "XXXX"] # 0.3055556
session_2_task$cs_rate_hard[session_2_task$id == "XXXX"] <- 0.22916667

# check old CR rate and then replace
session_2_task$cr_rate_hard[session_2_task$id == "XXXX"] # 0.8055556
session_2_task$cr_rate_hard[session_2_task$id == "XXXX"] <- 0.7916667
```

Identify participants who have one or more "unique errors" (UEs) in their responses (i.e., they pressed a button that does not correspond to a valid option).
```{r}
session_2_task %>%
  select(id, starts_with("ue_")) %>%
  filter_at(vars(-id), any_vars(. > 0)) 
```

The UE rates shown above are generally low. However, there are two participants with UE rates above our pre-stated thresholds: sub-XXXX and sub-XXXX. Sub-XXXX had UEs across multiple runs and, notably, their CR score was 0 (see below). They will therefore be excluded in subsequent steps. Sub-XXXX, by contrast, had UEs on one run only: hard run 1 [actually run 5]. The issue was spotted and corrected during scanning. Thus, replace values for CS and CR rate hard with this run removed.
```{r}
# check old CS rate and then replace
session_2_task$cs_rate_hard[session_2_task$id == "XXXX"] # 0.3125 
session_2_task$cs_rate_hard[session_2_task$id == "XXXX"] <- 0.3611111

# check old CR rate and then replace
session_2_task$cr_rate_hard[session_2_task$id == "XXXX"] # 0.6041667
session_2_task$cr_rate_hard[session_2_task$id == "XXXX"] <- 0.6944444
```

Filter out participants who did not provide at least one source correct response on the easy and hard task.
```{r}
session_2_task <- filter(session_2_task, cs_rate_easy != 0 & cs_rate_hard != 0)
```

Filter out participants who performed below chance in terms of correct rejections (1/6 = 0.16).
```{r}
session_2_task <- filter(session_2_task, cr_rate_easy >= 0.16 & cr_rate_hard >= 0.16)
```

Change task variable types to numeric.
```{r}
session_2_task <- session_2_task %>%
  mutate_at(vars(ends_with("easy")), as.numeric) %>%
  mutate_at(vars(ends_with("hard")), as.numeric) %>%
  mutate(s2_age = as.numeric(s2_age))
```

Run models regressing age on correct source, recognition, and misses.
```{r}
lm_cs_easy <- lm(cs_rate_easy ~ s2_age, data = session_2_task)
lm_cs_hard <- lm(cs_rate_hard ~ s2_age, data = session_2_task)
lm_recog_easy <- lm(recog_rate_easy ~ s2_age, data = session_2_task)
lm_recog_hard <- lm(recog_rate_hard ~ s2_age, data = session_2_task)
lm_miss_easy <- lm(misses_rate_easy ~ s2_age, data = session_2_task)
lm_miss_hard <- lm(misses_rate_hard ~ s2_age, data = session_2_task)
```

Calculate Cook's D for each regression model and store.
```{r}
cooks_d <- data.frame(id = session_2_task$id, 
                      cs_easy_d = cooks.distance(lm_cs_easy),
                      cs_hard_d = cooks.distance(lm_cs_hard),
                      recog_easy_d = cooks.distance(lm_recog_easy),
                      recog_hard_d = cooks.distance(lm_recog_hard),
                      miss_easy_d = cooks.distance(lm_miss_easy),
                      miss_hard_d = cooks.distance(lm_miss_hard))
```

For each measure (correct source, recognition, misses), determine whether a given participant's Cook D value is more than 3 standard deviations higher than the mean. After calculating these values, sum across the outlier columns. 
```{r}
cooks_d <- cooks_d %>%
  mutate(cs_easy_outlier = case_when(cs_easy_d >= (mean(cs_easy_d) + 3*sd(cs_easy_d)) ~ 1,
                                     cs_easy_d < (mean(cs_easy_d) + 3*sd(cs_easy_d)) ~ 0),
         cs_hard_outlier = case_when(cs_hard_d >= (mean(cs_hard_d) + 3*sd(cs_hard_d)) ~ 1,
                                     cs_hard_d < (mean(cs_hard_d) + 3*sd(cs_hard_d)) ~ 0),
         recog_easy_outlier = case_when(recog_easy_d >= (mean(recog_easy_d) + 3*sd(recog_easy_d)) ~ 1,
                                     recog_easy_d < (mean(recog_easy_d) + 3*sd(recog_easy_d)) ~ 0),
         recog_hard_outlier = case_when(recog_hard_d >= (mean(recog_hard_d) + 3*sd(recog_hard_d)) ~ 1,
                                     recog_hard_d < (mean(recog_hard_d) + 3*sd(recog_hard_d)) ~ 0),
         miss_easy_outlier = case_when(miss_easy_d >= (mean(miss_easy_d) + 3*sd(miss_easy_d)) ~ 1,
                                     miss_easy_d < (mean(miss_easy_d) + 3*sd(miss_easy_d)) ~ 0),
         miss_hard_outlier = case_when(miss_hard_d >= (mean(miss_hard_d) + 3*sd(miss_hard_d)) ~ 1,
                                     miss_hard_d < (mean(miss_hard_d) + 3*sd(miss_hard_d)) ~ 0)) %>%
  mutate(total_outliers = rowSums(across(ends_with("outlier")))) 
```

Checker whether any participants were deemed to be outliers on 3 or more measures.
```{r}
cooks_d %>% filter(total_outliers >= 3)
```

Remove all irrelevant objects from environment.
```{r}
rm(lm_cs_easy)
rm(lm_cs_hard)
rm(lm_miss_easy)
rm(lm_miss_hard)
rm(lm_recog_easy)
rm(lm_recog_hard)
rm(cooks_d)
```

Check to see if any of the remaining participants have CS/CR values that are 3 or more SDs from the mean.
```{r}
session_2_task %>% filter(cs_rate_easy < mean(cs_rate_easy) - (3*sd(cs_rate_easy)))
session_2_task %>% filter(cs_rate_hard < mean(cs_rate_hard) - (3*sd(cs_rate_hard)))
session_2_task %>% filter(cr_rate_easy < mean(cr_rate_easy) - (3*sd(cr_rate_easy))) 
session_2_task %>% filter(cr_rate_hard < mean(cr_rate_hard) - (3*sd(cr_rate_hard)))
```

Filter out these participants.
```{r}
session_2_task <- filter(session_2_task, !id %in% c(XXXX, XXXX, XXXX))
```

Remove participants who failed fMRI QC (checked separately using insert-file-name.xlsx). 
```{r}
session_2_imaging <- filter(session_2_task, !id %in% c(XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX))
```

Remove participants who had fewer than 8 events for correct source. This step is necessary for PLS analyses centered on CS (PLS requires 8+ events of interest).
```{r}
session_2_cs <- filter(session_2_imaging, num_cs_easy >= 8 & num_cs_hard >= 8) 
```

Remove participants who had fewer than 8 events for correct rejections. This step is necessary for PLS analyses centered on CR (PLS requires 8+ events of interest).
```{r}
session_2_cr <- filter(session_2_imaging, num_cr_easy >= 8 & num_cr_hard >= 8) 
```

# Export Data

Save Session 2 behavioural (task) data as SPSS file.
```{r}
write_sav(session_2_task, "insert-file-name.sav")
```

Save Session 2 imaging (CS) data as SPSS file.
```{r}
write_sav(session_2_cs, "insert-file-name.sav")
```

Save Session 2 imaging (CR) data as SPSS file.
```{r}
write_sav(session_2_cr, "insert-file-name.sav")
```
